thread:
Sam: DeployBot flagged a p95 regression on canary (slice=10%) ~2m ago. DeployBot: [AUTOMATION] Canary signal: p95 latency +38% vs baseline, error-rate x2, suggested action: pause rollout and evaluate for rollback. :warning:

Priya: Can we get quick evidence (graphs/traces) and which customer slices hit? don’t want to roll back without root cause. :eyes:

Marta: uploading screenshots in a sec — traces show KV cache misses spiking after the new kernel switch. Affected traffic = embeddings and small-chat routes, mostly eu-west region. I'm seeing 502 spikes in the same window.

Sam: thanks. DeployBot also attached the telemetry link: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/canary/7250001111 (p95, errors, traces).

DeployBot: [AUTOMATION] Action recommended: "pause_rollout". Auto-rollback not triggered (safety: human-confirm required for stateful change).

Jordan: Given KV cache incompatibility hypothesis, an automated rollback that reverts the kernel flag might leave clients with inconsistent caches. I prefer a manual, ticketed rollback so we can coordinate cache drains.

Priya: Agreed. Manual rollback + staged drain. Who can own execution? Sam, can you take operator?

Sam: I can run it. Will follow runbook and create a dedicated rollback ticket. Drafting rollback ticket now: ROLLBACK-7250.

Oncall-Bot: @here oncall rota: Marta is primary (EU), Jordan is secondary. Please route action items via the ticket.

Marta: I'll coordinate cache-drain. Plan: 1) Pause rollout traffic split. 2) Pin traffic to previous model/kernel. 3) Drain KV cache on nodes with new flag. 4) Validate synthetic p95 and error-rate. 5) Unpin if stable.

Priya: Good. Include communications steps: internal slack banner + short customer email for affected enterprise tenants. Draft release-note blurb once we decide.

Sam: Pasting the manual rollback snippet from runbook (will paste to ROLLBACK-7250):

```
# Pause rollout (traffic API)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/rollouts/7250/pause -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY"

# Pin to previous kernel+model version
deployctl pin --deployment inference-prod --to-version 2026-03-21-kernel-a1

# Trigger graceful drain on nodes with flag
nodes=$(infractl list-nodes --label kernel=a1-new)
for n in $nodes; do infractl drain $n --wait 300; done

# Validate metrics
curl https://telemetry.redwood.internal/validate?canary=0.1
```

Jordan: That looks good. One extra step: run a small smoke suite against embeddings for the top 3 affected customers before full traffic shift.

Sam: Will run smoke. ETA ~10m to prepare commands and start.

Marta: I'll prep the customer comm template. Suggest sending to affected customers with subject: "Temporary degradation detected — rollback in progress" and cc: accounts for enterprise SLAs.

Priya: Approving manual rollback execution. Sam, you have authority to execute ROLLBACK-7250. Please post progress in this thread and tag @Oncall-Bot when starting so we record timeline. :white_check_mark:

Sam: Starting now. tagging Oncall-Bot. Executing step 1: pause rollout.

DeployBot: [SYSTEM] Rollout 7250 paused by Sam. Traffic split set to 0% new.

Sam: Step 2: pin to previous kernel+model. Running deployctl pin...

DeployBot: [SYSTEM] Pin successful: inference-prod -> 2026-03-21-kernel-a1.

Sam: Step 3: draining nodes with new flag. Running infractl drain.

Marta: Observing drain progress. 3/5 nodes drained, KV miss rate dropping on drained nodes.

Jordan: Running smoke tests against customer slices now. Sending results: all three smoke tests ✅ for embeddings, no regressions.

Sam: Step 4: validating telemetry. p95 back to within 5% of baseline, error-rate returned to normal for canary slice.

Priya: Great. Next: public comms. Marta, please send internal slack banner and email draft to accounts. Keep wording explanatory but concise.

Marta: Internal banner posted in #prod-notices. Draft email saved to ROLLBACK-7250: "We detected a transient latency spike affecting embeddings and small-chat in eu-west during today's rollout. We paused the rollout and reverted to the previous kernel. Your traffic should see normal behavior now. We are investigating root cause and will follow up with postmortem."

Sam: Step 5: after 10m of stable telemetry, we'll unpin and do a controlled re-roll of the kernel flag as a canary patch (smaller slice, monitor closely). For now we'll leave pin in place until postmortem.

Priya: Agreed. Also add a note to release notes: "hotfix: reverted kernel flag due to p95 regression on canary; monitoring and postmortem forthcoming."

DeployBot: [SYSTEM] ROLLBACK-7250 ticket updated: status=done, owner=Sam, timeline attached.

Sam: Marking this thread resolved. Final checks: telemetry stable for 12m, customer comms sent, ticket ROLLBACK-7250 created and closed with follow-up assigned to Marta for the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :bow:
